title: Christ’s death as sacrifice and redemption-price
source_text: XII. Et hinc quoque est quod Scriptura Sacra de morte Christi frequenter loquitur, ceu de sacrificio quo peccata nostra fuerunt expiata; ut praesertim videre est in epistola ad Hebraeos, & apud Isaiam cap. jam citato; ubi dicitur Messias animam suam posuisse oblationem pro peccato. Ac praeterea tanquam de pretio quo sumus a morte & perditione redempti: ut quum dicit Paulus Christum se ipsum αντιλυτρον dedisse pro omnibus. Et Christus ipse, Filium hominis non venisse ut sibi ministretur, sed ut ministret, detque animam suam in redemptionis pretium pro multis. Unde est quod Petrus affirmat nos non fuisse redemptos corruptibilibus, auro, & argento, sed pretioso sanguine agni immaculati & incontaminati Christi.
pass_a_gloss: Hence also Sacred Scripture frequently speaks of Christ’s death as of a sacrifice by which our sins were expiated—as is especially to be seen in the epistle to the Hebrews and in Isaiah in the chapter already cited, where the Messiah is said to have made his soul an offering for sin. And further as of a price by which we were redeemed from death and perdition: as when Paul says Christ gave himself as a ransom for all; and Christ himself, that the Son of man came not to be served but to serve and to give his soul as a redemption-price for many. Hence Peter affirms that we were not redeemed with corruptible things, gold and silver, but with the precious blood of Christ, the spotless and unblemished lamb.
pass_b_english: Scripture casts Christ’s death as expiating sacrifice and redeeming price.
He gave himself as ransom; we are bought with his precious blood, not gold.
